correctness.rationale: For char 2, n>=11 congruent 3 mod 8, check the generating-series derivative cubic and translation invariance via Lucas parity. With three distinct coordinate values translate one to zero: comparing the cubic roots forces nonzero multiplicities 1 mod 4, and e4 forces 1 mod 8; the zero block is also 1 mod 8. Two values reduce to binomial(a,3), binomial(a-1,3), binomial(a,4), whose joint vanishing gives a mod 8 in {1,2}, hence a refinement to three 1-mod-8 blocks. Converse follows from generating functions. Irreducibility follows by primitive linear induction for e2,e3,e4 and explicit nondivisibility specializations. The Hessian is block diagonal and has rank n-3 at generic three-distinct-value points; dimension two plus hypersurface Cohen-Macaulay gives normality. The exact standalone checker passes GF4 n11,n19 and incidence tests; finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

originality.rationale: Xie (2026) covers top-dimensional partition planes, dimension, generic Hessian; those are not new. The independently proved added implication that every singular point lies on those planes eliminates any lower-dimensional reduced components in this full arithmetic family, a conclusion not supplied by the inspected Xie theorem statements and identified as an unclassified issue in Xie Section 7. Orzel treats dimension bounds; Cafure et al. give partition containment. published-finding corpus and literature searches found no exact equivalent; implicit/unindexed coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: A global general theorem not identified in available indexes could imply the complete-support assertion without matching wording.

value.rationale: The complete reduced singular support (not just dimension or maximal components) of a natural infinite family of normal positive-characteristic quartic hypersurfaces is explicitly classified. The novel no-hidden-components implication excludes residual curves and isolated components and yields the full pure-plane singular arrangement, with a concrete 55-plane, 495-line-pair incidence configuration at n=11. It addresses a meaningful gap left by the previously known extremal component theorem; finite counts and generic Hessian facts alone are not the asserted value.
